text.description: Macro Friendly Crispy Chicken Sandwich  Per sandwich: 440 Calories 50g Protein* 43g Carbs 6g Fat Weight: ~12 ounces  Chick-fil-A Version: 440 calories 29g Protein 41g Carbs 17g Fat Weight: ~6.5 ounces  In other words - my version is DOUBLE the size, almost double the protein, 1/3 the fat content, for the same calories as the chick fil a sandwich. And in my opinion - it tastes much better too  *Also - in the video I said it contains “almost 50g of protein” 😅 - because I forgot to include the sauce in the initial macro calculation. The sriracha sauce adds ~5g of protein to each sandwich!  Ingredients:  One ~12oz chicken breast, halved  Salt + garlic powder  **Dipping stations** Station 1: Flour + salt/garlic/pepper Station 2: Egg whites + hot sauce Station 3: Crushed corn flakes  NOTE: I don’t measure the amount of each ingredient added to each station as it’s typically easier to add excess in order to ensure complete coating. I weighed the amount that stuck to each piece of chicken in order to calculate the macronutrients. text.description: ⚡️FOR THUNDER THIGHS⚡️ Here’s how you can train hamstrings intelligently 1️⃣ Typically I’ll train them 2 days per week. Day 1 is a lying leg curl + a stiff leg deadlift variation. Day 2 is often only a seated curl (this is because it on my more quad focused leg day) 2️⃣ Everything is usually for 3-4 sets in the 6-12 rep range with at least 3 minutes of rest between each set 3️⃣ If I’m doing both a leg curl and a SLDL variation in the same workout, I’ll usually start with the leg curl. In which case, it’ll be a lying leg curl (Lying leg curls will train the hamstrings in their short position & SLDL’s will train them in their lengthened position. This leaves seated leg curls to be done on my 2nd day as the stand-alone hamstring exercise.) — I hope this gives you some direction in your training. text.description: I was a Senior Staff Physician prescribing hormones that were custom tailored to our clients bodies. All the guys who worked there were on testosterone cream. I sat down in this chair in the morning and remember the arms of the chair were slippery. I thought it might be polish or something. Throughout the day I noticed my body was behaving strangely. I was becoming increasingly more turned on and looking at my coworkers like I had not before… it was so alarming I had to avoid them and focus on my computer the entire day. Suffice to say the experience was telling. It made me realize what men go through with high testosterone levels. How this changes your entire worldview. This video was actually so triggering to hyper-masculine men that a well known influencer claimed I made the whole thing up. I think it hits a nerve for this guy. My goal wasn’t to blame men for how much hormones affect their lives or behavior, but to illuminate how women don’t totally understand the masculine experience… because we have different hormones. I have a high libido to begin with so when my levels were raised to supra-normal levels it became really intense. What most people don’t realize is testosterone replacement is often used for women with low libido. I actually think it would be a really fun experiment to run a study where men get dosed with a large amount of estrogen and women get dosed with a large amount of testosterone for a day & they have to reflect on how these hormones change their perception of reality. Someone told me that they once got their wife’s estrogen and progesterone cream on their skin and it totally made him cry at a movie normally wouldn’t have made him so emotional. Food for thought, folks. #testosterone #health #Fitness #trt #steroids #drmolly

text.description: High Protein Honey Garlic Butter Chicken Mac n Cheese!🍗🍯🧀 Absolutely one of the best combos, so indulgent, bursting with flavour and packed with 60g of protein! Macros Per Serving (4 Total) 597 Calories | 59g Protein | 52g Carbs | 16g Fat Ingredients (Makes 4) Honey Garlic Chicken - 800g Raw Chicken Breast cut into cubes - 1.5 Tsp Salt - 1 Tsp Black Pepper - 1 Tsp Chilli Flakes (leave it out if you don’t want it spicy) - 1.5 Tsp Garlic Powder - 1.5 Tsp Onion Powder - 1.5 Tep Paprika or Smoked Paprika - 2 Tsp Olive Oil - 30g Light Butter (Brand: Lurpak) for cooking + extra once cooked - 2 Tsp Minced Garlic - 30g Honey (15g Honey per batch of chicken) - Handful Fresh Chopped Parsley Get a pan on medium heat first then add butter. Let it melt then add your chicken (don’t overcrowd the pan). Cook for 4-5 mins on one side first till you get a nice golden brown crust. Then cook the other side for 3-4 mins more. Lower the heat completely when adding the extra butter, garlic and honey. Mix till well coated and sticky then set aside Garlic Mac n Cheese - Big Tbsp Minced Garlic - 300ml Skimmed Milk - 160g Light Cream Cheese (Brand: Philadelphia) - 1 Tsp Salt or to taste - 1/2 Tsp Black Pepper - 1 Tsp Smoked Paprika - 1/2 Tsp Nutmeg (adds a great deep flavour!) - 100g Low Fat Cheddar Cheese (You can use any low fat cheese you have available) - 220g Uncooked Macaroni Pasta or any pasta of your choice On medium low heat cook the minced garlic in the residue butter of the chicken for 2 mins till fragrant. Then add milk, cream cheese, spices. Mix this till completely smooth then lower the heat before adding the cheddar cheese. Stir till it melts then add your cooked macaroni and give it a good mix then Serve & ENJOY! . . . . #garlicbutter #honeygarlic #chicken #chickenrecipes #macncheese #macaroni #pasta #macandcheese #highprotein #mealprep #foodie #healthyrecipes #weightloss #lowcalorie #eathealthy #fitness #mealprepideas

text.description: Chili Cheese Fries   Use this recipe as a reminder - the way your food looks doesn’t dictate whether it’s something that can fit in your diet. text.description: How to fix skinny-fat🙃 “Skinny-fat” is confusing? Because the more weight you try and lose, the worse the problem seems to get? That’s usually because people are trying to solve the wrong problem💡 The problem most people *think* they need to solve is having too much body fat. They try and solve this by: - adding endless cardio - and restricting food more and more But that’s only going to make the problem worse Because “skinny-fat” doesn’t usually come from not having too much body fat, it comes from not having enough *muscle* underneath our fat to give us any shape or definition. To fix this, you would want to: - Focus on lifting heavy weights - Actually limit your cardio (probably not more than 1/3 of your total exercise) - And often times actually eat *more* food, not less It’s also important to note that every human body is different, so the exact solution for each person will be a little bit different - but this generally a good place to start 🤘🏼 #skinnyfat #abs #coreworkout #cardio #FitTok

To fix this, you would want to: - Focus on lifting heavy weights - Actually limit your cardio (probably not more than 1/3 of your total exercise) - And often times actually eat *more* food, not less It’s also important to note that every human body is different, so the exact solution for each person will be a little bit different - but this generally a good place to start 🤘🏼 #skinnyfat #abs #coreworkout #cardio #FitTok

text.description: Hate to burst your bubble (or maybe rings in this case? lol) But any device that tells you how many calories you burned during a workout is simply not even close to the truth. (p.s. congrats sam, you killed it this weekend) Devices like the Apple Watch, Whoop, Oura, etc. are great for certain things (e.g. step count, sleep data, recovery) But they suck for figuring out how many calories you burn Yes, the technology in these devices has gotten better since this study came out a few years ago… But the technology isn’t why they’re innacurate Here’s what the calorie tracking device takes into account to give you an estimate of how many calories you burn: - Heart rate - Gender - Weight - Age - Workout type But what it would take to *accurately* estimate how many calories you burn during a workout is all of that, PLUS 100+ other things that these devices can’t take into account… Things like your hormone profile and genetics, to even more ridiculous things like the temperature of the room you’re in or how much sleep you got last night… But that’s okay… Because knowing *exactly* how many calories you burned in one workout doesn’t really matter The amount of calories you burn in your workouts is <5% of what you burn in an entire week So if you’re trying to lose weight, adjusting your calorie intake day by day doesn’t really make any sense And it would make a lot more sense by just paying attention to your calorie intake and comparing it to how your scale is moving over time e.g. if you are eating 2,200 calories consistently, and the scale isn’t moving, then 2,200 is around your maintenence and you should either eat below that or increase how many calories you burn in a day to get into a deficit Study mentioned in reel: PMID: 28538708 #FitTok #GymTok #Running

text.description: Twinkies make you… healthy?   Not quite 💔 (even though that’s what half the comments will tell you that’s what I’m saying) Sometimes you need extreme examples to highlight a point Should anyone eat like this to lose weight? No—short term health improvement is not the same thing as long term health outcomes  But there are 3 BIG lessons I think you can take from the experiment in this video: 1. A calorie deficit isn’t *a* way you lose weight, it’s *the* way you lose weight 2. Simply getting to a healthy body weight and not carrying excess body fat will probably do more for your health than any “optimal” diet would staying at a higher body fat level 3. And as terrifying as some influencers make certain “junk” foods sound for your health, there’s really no such thing as a healthy or unhealthy food - only a healthy or unhealthy diet as a whole. Someone who’s diet consists of 95% fast food that eats one salad isn’t “healthy” And someone who eats mostly whole, minimally processed foods having a donut for a snack isn’t “unhealhty” On top of all of this, its a nice remider that your diet only accounts for roughly ~20% of your overall health Things like your body composition, how much strength you have, how active you are, how well you sleep, and how well you manage your stress, along with 100+ other things also go into it And yes, I know what you’re thinking… This is just one guy who did a self experiment, you can’t use this as evidence Which I agree with But there is PLENTY of research showing that simply reducing body fat levels, regaradless of how it’s done, improves so many different health metrics Like: - type 2 diabetes - hypertension (high blood pressure) - cholesterol and lipid levels - cardiovascular disease - improved glycemic control and reduced insulin resistance - and more (research linked below) ___ https://doi.org/10.7326/0003-4819-149-7-200810070-01004 PMID: 35457744 PMID: 28214525 PMID: 12055705 PMID: 21463847 PMID: 21593294 #gym #fittok #gymtok #weightloss #seedoils

text.description: No, the aspartame in diet coke is not going to kill you If you want an easy way to tell who is full of s*** on this app, remember this one principle: The dose makes the poison For everything When someone at the grocery store tells you to avoid certain everyday items because they contain an ingredient you can’t pronounce, they often leave out a key detail: HOW MUCH of that ingredient is actually in the product Because everything… has a safe, and a toxic dose This applies not just to mysterious ingredients, but even to things we consider healthy, like water, vitamins, and minerals. Take water for example: We all know it’s good for us But while a single drop does nothing, drinking 1 liter of water every hour all day can lead to water toxicity - where you essentially drown from the inside out Why this is so funny to me - is that the amount of coke zero someone would need to consume in order for the aspartame to become potentially dangerous… Would be around 48, 12oz cans (for someone my size) 48, 12oz cans = 17 liters of liquid The toxic dose for water in one day = 10-15 liters  i.e. YOU WOULD DIE FASTER FROM THE WATER IN THE COKE ZEROS BEFORE THE ASPARTAME EVER GAVE YOU A SINGLE HEALTH RISK #FitTok #GymTok #health #dietcoke #organic  References: PMID: 30602577

text.description: Fat burning ≠ Fat loss 😯 Yes, there is such a thing as a “fat-burning zone” But no, it doesn’t matter at all when it comes to actually losing fat ☹️ There’s one BIG problem with thinking that spending more time in the “fat-burning zone” will result in more fat lost… When you burn more fat and less carbs during a workout, you just burn less fat and more carbs later in the day (and vice-versa) This happens because your body “calibrates” how much body fat and carbohydrates you burn over a 24-hour period so that you burn the same amount of each over time, regardless of what you burn during your workouts. For example: Whether you burn 500 calories doing sprints for 30-minutes, with most of those calories coming from carbs OR 500 calories from a 90 minute incline walk, with most of those calories coming from fat You’ll still burn about the same amount of body fat at the end of the day So basically, how much fat you *lose* in response to a cardio workout depends on how much it’s adding to your calorie deficit - not how much fat you burned for energy during the workout Fat *loss* comes down to storing less fat than you burn over time And that comes from whether or not you’re in a calorie deficit Incline walking IS NOT BAD!! I actually prefer it over sprints. It’s easier on the body, it takes less recovery, and for most people it doesn’t increase hunger that much - making it a great option if you’re trying to lose weight It’s just not inherently better than any other form of cardio for fat loss… It comes down to what you can be consistent with, and what you actually enjoy (or hate less lol) Studies/Research: 24-hour fat loss calibration: PMID: 15896087 #fittok #12330 #fatburner #gym

text.description: READ THIS FIRST!!! (pwetty plz🥺) This is a 60-second clip, from a full 60-minute podcast where we break down Strength Standards So let’s start by saying - there are countless other factors that go into how challenging an exercise is *other than just your height* The estimated 10-20% harder on the bench press (like stated in the video) is just one example of many used in the podcast That’s also assuming that the two individuals had: - the same exact amount of muscle mass - the same exact muscle insertion points - the same exact shoulder structure - the same exact joint angles - the same exact muscle belly lengths - the same exact other limb proportions - the same exact form/technique - and about 100 other metrics And where longer arms may be a disadvantage on bench press, they would be an advantage on deadlifts since it would shorten the range of motion making the deadlift a bit easier So I am NOT saying that being 2 inches taller makes every exercise you do 10-20% harder I am just highlighting that your skeletal anatomy plays a role in how strong you are The full podcast is live on Spotify, Apple Podcast, and YouTube if you want to listen more about how your anatomy affects your strength Added notes: 1. This is not a post about using height (tall or short) as an excuse or saying that one is inherently better than the other. This is to help understand basic biomechanics that you can implement into your own training routine based on your anatomy. For example: I generally have athletes with longer limbs work in lower rep ranges for bench press than those with shorter arms (i.e. 2-4 or 3-5 vs. 4-6 or 5-7 in strength training). This adjustment allows them to avoid building up excessive fatigue, recover, and perform better. Different exercises would have different adjustments based on other anatomical differences. One’s not better than the other, it’s data you can use to improve your approach, that’s all👍🏽 #tall #short #shortking #samsulek #fittok

text.description: Fuel for your leg day 😈 Here’s what you need to know: 1. You can use squat shoes on leg press to help get more range of motion, however, let’s be real. Most people aren’t bringing squats shoes to the gym. 2. You can do reverse banded hack squats to even out the resistance profile of the exercise. But again let’s be real, MOST people aren’t doing that & that’s not the focus of the video. 3. Sissy squats - WATCH MY SISSY SQUAT VIDEO - they take practice. It will show how you can progress them over time. They take practice. They are my favorite quad exercise. 4. Are there other great exercises for the quads? Yes, but these are all you would ever need. Barbell squats didn’t make the list? No. Although they’re a great exercise and obviously can help you grow your quads, they are not the best when compared to the leg press, hack squat, and pendulum squat. With squats, there are many potential outside factors that can cause your quads to not get the best stimulus for growth. For instance, maybe your low back gets tired before your quads do, and as a result, your form breaks down. Issues like this are not a concern with the exercises shown in this video. I am not saying “never do barbell squats”. I think it’s a great thing for every lifter to be proficient at them. You can get very good results from them. #bodybuilding #legday #legdayworkout #quads #quadworkout #legs #gym #Fitness #workout #legpress #hacksquat #legextension #bodybuildingtips  #davisdiley

text.description: "Calisthenics can't build muscle" - a gentlemanly debate. --- Calisthenics can absolutely build muscle, and you can use different variations to find the ideal difficulty for you. Interestingly, this might ESPECIALLY apply to larger lifters as well as smaller beginners. The larger people have more bodyweight attached to them (even if it's muscle). 10 pullups for a 250lb bodybuilder, for example, is awesome. And beginners generally have more room to grow, regardless of what they use. That said, there's no reason you can't or shouldn't use weights. Weights and machines offer new angles and positions that you make not be able to mimic exactly with bodyweight exercise. They allow you overload without changing your movement. This may be helpful to people who want to specialize in certain areas. However, it should be noted that you can develop an athletic physique with calisthenics and many have done so (for a variety of reasons).  This is part of a new "Arguing With Myself" series that emphatically argues different sides of an issue to (hopefully) give a slightly more nuanced understanding of it. The ones prior have been longer and it's hard to fit all important context into a Short. This one was fun to make though, and I used it to test my new mic. Have a great day! #homeworkout #hybridcalisthenics

text.description: Why are some people strong at one thing but "fail" at others?  I occasionally see people laughing at bodybuilders supposedly failing at doing muscle ups or even pushups. While these movements don't always look clean, I always think that they can learn them relatively quickly if they want. The foundation of strength and muscle may already be there.  Strength is at least somewhat skill specific. That's why if you stop doing a lift for a while, your numbers might drop and then rise rapidly when you start practicing it again.  A few potential lessons we can take from this:  1.) Our training should be close to what we want to improve. This can be anything from sport-specific movements to daily functions (think squatting for standing up, step ups for climbing stairs, running for running, etc.)  2.) We can add a few minutes of variations after our main workouts as accessories if we want to maintain a broader variety of skills while still focusing on our primary exercises. Mobility plays a large role here, so try to incorporate a large, full range of motion within at least some exercise.  The good news is that, with even small amounts of practice, there's more crossover than we might think. The example I gave of 400lb squats VS one-leg squats - sometimes this can be learned in a few sessions of practice. There are other factors like joint health and mobility, but this is covered under the specificity of training.  Sorry if some parts are not as clear as other times. Some parts of our team are sick this time of year, so we tried to do some simpler productions 😅. Still hope this can help. Have a wonderful day!  #hybridcalisthenics #homeworkout

text.description: How to Squat on the Smith Machine: Proper Bar Positioning for Stronger and Safer Lifts. If you are familiar with the conventional Barbell squat, the Smith machine squat should be a walk in the park. Keep the bar in the middle of your body to avoid straining your lower back. Don’t sacrifice form for a supposed Glute stretch! Stand with your feet hip-width apart, and your toes slightly angled outward to open up your hips. Keep your feet under the barbell and not too far from the bar. I hope this helps 🦾 #squats #legs #legday #legdayworkout #fitnesstips #workouttips #workoutroutine #smithmachine

text.description: Hamstrings 101 1️⃣ Typically, I’ll train them 2 days per week. Day 1 is a lying leg curl + a stiff leg deadlift variation. Day 2 is often only a seated curl (this is because it’s on my more quad focused leg day) 2️⃣ Everything is usually for 2-4 sets in the 5-12 rep range with at least 3 minutes of rest between each set 3️⃣ If I’m doing both a leg curl and a SLDL variation in the same workout, I’ll usually start with the leg curl. In which case, it’ll be a lying leg curl (Lying leg curls will train the hamstrings in their short position & SLDL’s will train them in their lengthened position. This leaves seated leg curls to be done on my 2nd day as the stand-alone hamstring exercise.) I really hope this helps give you some sort of direction in your training. text.description: Hip Abduction Machine Tutorial: Proper technique and targeting the glutes. The seated hip abduction machine isolates the muscles of the outer hip and thigh, including the gluteus medius & minimus and parts of the gluteus Maximus.  Often times people lean forward thinking they’re targeting their glutes but that’s not the case. The key is to sit upright or back in the chair, rather than leaning forward in order to effectively engage the glute muscles. You’ll notice that you’re not able to do much weight because you’re not just swinging the weights out and in but instead controlling it which will help you engage the muscles more. Give this tip a try and lemme know how it goes. I hope this helps 💪🏿 #glutes #abduction #fitnesstips #workouttips #fitnessmotivation #legday #strengthtraining

text.description: Leg extensions 🤝  ✅ make sure the machine is set up for your body, the back rest should be adjusted so that your knees line up with the pivot point, the ankle pad should be sitting at your ankles and set to the deepest range of motion.  ✅ next make sure your knees are lined up with your hips, you can do this by pointing your toes straight up, this will stop them from rotating out or inward and take tension off your knees.  ✅ keep your lower back and glutes glued to the back rest and seat, pull yourself down into it and engage your core, don’t over arch your lower back.  ✅ don’t just swing the weight around and use a ton of momentum, pick a weight that’s challenging but that you can control. This is the only machine that works your quads in the fully shortened position, so slow down your reps, really squeeze your quads at the top and then control the eccentric. text.description: The end hits hard 😮‍💨 Keep showing up. I started my fitness journey as someone who felt super insecure in herself, had no one supporting her and pretty much ZERO confidence. text.description: The day I found out I was pregnant I made a promise to myself that I would do all I could do be the best possible version of me.. for me. And my baby. I made a promise to myself to protect me and my baby, to stay active, and live as healthy as I possibly could. 🤟🏽 with my doctors permission of course.  With that being said. Pregnancy has brought so many ups and downs. So many days where I was able to get up, move, do cardio, eat healthy, workout like I used to. And so many days where I was down, nauseous, sleeping, and could barely get out of bed and felt so unlike myself. I learned quickly that I wasn’t going to be perfect this pregnancy. I wasn’t going to be the old me. But a new me. Who allows myself grace, who is growing a human, and who is trying her absolute best everyday. 🩵 To all my pregnant mamas out there. All of our journeys are so different, all of our journeys are so beautiful, and this is a reminder to never compare toanother’s journey. Whether you are moving your body every day, or just trying your best to get out of bed and make it through your day. We are in this together. THIS IS YOUR JOURYNEY, Your body, your baby. Don’t let anyone cloud your journey. 🤟🏽 do what is best for you.  I’m so grateful for this miracle in my life. And I cannot wait to be a mama. I’ve been doing my volume 9 volume throughout the last 19 weeks of my pregnancy and I feel so empowered and strong. Volume 9 will be available on my app tomorrow. 🎀 ( keep your eye out. There will be an early bird sale for those who purchase early)  Xo.  #Fitness #trending #fitnessmotivation #explorepage #pregnancy #pregnancyjourney #relatable #newmom #strengthtraining #motivation

text.description: The most common question I get is, “How did you lose all this weight?”  Here’s how I did it: 1. Move Your Body: I committed to strength training at least 4-6 times a week, followed by 30 minutes of cardio—whether it’s on the treadmill, stairs, or elliptical. 2. Fuel Your Body: Please, do not starve yourself! It’s all about balance: aim for 80% healthy meals and 20% of whatever you love—in moderation. 3. Stay Hydrated: Drink at least 2-3 liters of water daily. You’d be surprised at how underrated water is! 4. Be Consistent: Consistency is key! No matter the challenges, don’t quit. Remember, progress takes time, and every step counts! These principles have been my go-to for weight loss. text.description: If you're like when I started...gym anxiety made you quiet working our and pursuing your fitness goals again and again. These are three facts that reduced my gym anxiety and finally got me consistent with working out. 1.) no one cares about you. i used to be super skinny and had a lot of gym anxiety. i felt like i was embarrassing myself by going to the gym not looking fit. years later, i now know that 99% of people do not even see you. everyones trying to get in and out of the gym because they have somewhere to be and are busy. plus think about it: how many people are really thinking about you when they're in the middle of lifting really challenging weights? sometimes i cant even remember how many reps i did 2.) progress takes time. i gave up so many times bc i didnt look any different a few weeks into working out. it really sucks because if i kept at it for longer than 1-2 months i would've started seeing so much growth from then on out 3.) use videos. not knowing if i looked stupid doing an exercise wrong really messed with my confidence at the gym. but thats why i make videos explaining exercise form to yall. theres also soooo many videos out there now for you to bring to the gym to watch and copy to master form! but just make sure to try your best to separate good info from the BS! #fitnessjourney #gymanxiety #confidence #gymmotivation #motivation #fitnessmotivation #gym #fitness

text.description: By far, one of my favorite interactions to ever happen to me. Just like you, I’m human. I have my struggles, insecurities, and moments of doubt. The only difference is I have a large following — which brings both incredible support and relentless scrutiny. Because I don’t fit the typical “fitness influencer” mold, and I don’t edit my videos to erase my cellulite, I get plenty of comments and messages telling me I need to lose weight or calling me fat. Most of the time, I brush it off, laugh, or block people. But sometimes, it does get to me. This past week was tough, and I had to remind myself that these skewed opinions mean nothing. Then, the universe sent me a little encouragement. First, a coworker walked up to me mid-workout and said, “You look snatched, girl!” The second was a wholesome interaction with Marilyn Gold, a woman who didn’t know me at all but admired me just as I am. Her words? “Keep THAT body of yours.” Her kindness hit me deeply. She saw me — the real me — not for some idealized standard but for my strength and presence. It reminded me of why I’m here: to help change the narrative about what fitness looks like. Fitness isn’t about perfection or fitting into a mold. It’s about showing up, building strength, and honoring your unique journey. So, to anyone who’s ever felt out of place or doubted their worth in this space: keep going. Your body, your story, and your value aren’t up for debate. Strength is more than aesthetics, and you are already powerful. Let’s rewrite the narrative together. #BodyPositive #RealNotPerfect #FitnessForAll #StrongNotSkinny #SelfLoveJourney #FitnessMotivation #HealthAtEverySize #EmbraceYourBody #BodyDiversity #ChangeTheNarrative #YouAreEnough #ConfidenceIsKey #LoveYourself #MindsetMatters #BreakTheMold

text.description: If you are looking to build muscle, make sure you’re doing this…. ⏲️ Take MORE time in between your sets! Stop moving so fast, and only taking 30-60 seconds. There’s PLENTY of research that suggests that more rest time, leads to more hypertrophy. 💪 The ideal rest time? 90 seconds.  If you’re performing compound strength movements, I’d recommend 2 minutes or more.  This will maximize your recovery in between your sets, so you can then increase your weight for reps during your entire workout.  So unless you’re trying to be super skinny or focus on building endurance… ✅ Start taking more rest time! #fitness #mensfitness #buildmuscle #gymhacks #fitnesstips

text.description: Is the "viral salmon bowl" recipe a good alternative to eating normal salmon?  Recently, my girl told me she wanted to try this new viral recipe for a salmon rice bowl. I had my doubts but we decided to make it. We got some atlantic salmon and seasoned it with lemon peper and salt and put it in the airfrier.  While that was sitting we got the ingredients to season, some kewpie mayo, soy sauce, and some knock off siracha. Then we put the rice in the rice cooker. That’s it. I had a feeling this wasn’t really going to taste good because there’s so little effort that goes into it, but let me just shut up for a sec cuz damn I was wrong.  The salmon came out oozin and golden brown. The rice was ready  too and we put in the siracha, kewpie mayo, soy sauce and mashed it up. Looks kinda whatever right? I thought so too until we sat down and started eating. Wrapped it with some seaweed and wow. Best thing is it’s 570 calories and 30 grams of protein and it keeps you surprisingly full. Her dog would not stop asking for some, but sorry I ended up eating it all.  Since, then my girl has been making it every other day for lunch and has been loving it so yall should try it too! #fitnesstips #salmon #salmonrice #salmonbowl #highprotein #highproteinmeals #lowcalorie #lowcalorierecipe #fish #diettips #weightloss #caloriedeficit

text.description: The "secret" to how I grew my arms👇 My arms have grown more from doing less. I’ve been getting told  that my arms are a big strongpoint in my physique. But it’s funny because my arms barely grew the first 2 years of working out and were always a weakpoint. So what changed? I used to do 3 tricep exercises: rope pushdowns, straight bar pushdowns, and skull crushers. I also did 3 bicep exercises: ez bar curls, hammer curls, and cable curls. For all exercises I did 3-4 sets and 8-12 reps.  Now I only do 3 exercises total: tricep rope pushdowns, standing bicep curls, and hammer curls with each being only 1-3 sets and 6-10 reps. It’s nearly a third of the volume, but instead my intensity has gone up. Each set looks like this, and is taken to failure. Each rep has intent and controlled eccentrics and powerful concentrics. After doing just 1-3 sets of each, there is no way I can physically push myself more because I’m completely tapped out. I credit efficient and intense training to blowing up my arms over anything else. If you’re not seeing much growth in your arms, try playing around with how much volume you have. It might just be that you doing more is what’s preventing faster progress. #fitnesstips #gymtips #workout #armworkout #bicepsworkout #tricepsworkout #tricep #bicep

text.description: What's the BEST workout routine & how many days should you workout? 👇  Anyone that gives you a straight up answer isn't always right. In reality, it depends. We all recover at different rates, require different amounts of weekly volume, and all train differently. Taking this into account, there is no best workout routine. But that doesn't mean you can't make your workout routine the best for you. Doing so actually makes you find way more progress not only because you're literally optimizing your routine, but also because yiu're able to be really consistent with it.  1.) Find the right amount of weekly set volume (somewhere between 6-20 weekly sets per muscle group) you need to recover fully from each workout while still challenging yourself.  2.) Find how many days a week you can be realitically most consistent with. Whether it's 4,5,6 times a week, space out rest days accordingly to be able to recover from your previous workouts to prevent any performance issues. Then assign a variety of splits: Push Pull Legs (6 days), Push Pull Legs Upper Lower (5 days), Upper Lower (4 days) 3.) Find exercises that are smarter than others and effective at targeting the muscle you're aiming to target.  4.) Now that you have the workout routine, sets, and exercises, it all comes down to finding a good rep range for your exercises. Any rep range between 6-15 is ideal. I personally love 6-8 or 6-10 for most of my exercises. You're welcome. You're welcome. Now you've got almost everything it takes to actually have the BEST workout routine. All it takes now is to test and fine tune 😌 #fitnesstips #workoutroutine #workoutplan #gymtips #buildingmuscle

text.description: Straight Arm Lat Pulldown Technique: Perfecting your form for Maximum results.  The emphasis should be on feeling the entire range of motion, not the amount of weight you use on the exercise. Grab the handle with a pronated grip (double overhand) at roughly shoulder width and lean forward slightly by hinging at the hips. Keep the elbow slightly flexed and initiate the movement by Pulling the bar to your thigh until the lats are fully contracted and then slowly lower under control. text.description: 🔽 등운동(Back Workout) 그립별 자극 차이점 🔽 🔸Back Training – Grip Differences & Prime Movers 1. 와이드 그립 랫 풀다운 (Wide-Grip Lat Pulldown) - 팔을 넓게 벌려 바를 잡고 아래로 당기면, 광배근 상부(upper lats)를 집중적으로 자극한다. 2. 뉴트럴 그립 시티드 로우 (Neutral-Grip Seated Row) - 손바닥이 마주보는 핸들을 사용해 당기면 팔의 궤도가 자연스럽고 안정적으로 유지되어 등 중부(middle back)를 자극한다. 3. 와이드 뉴트럴 그립 시티드 로우 (Wide-Neutral Grip Seated Row) - 팔을 넓게 벌려 중립 그립으로 당기면 광배근 외측과 등 두께(outer lats & back thickness)를 동시에 자극한다. 4 뉴트럴 그립 랫 풀다운 (Neutral-Grip Lat Pulldown) - 손바닥이 서로 마주보게 잡고 당기면 광배근 하부(lower lats)에 자극이 들어간다. #backworkout #latsworkout #latpulldown #backday  #fitnesstips #tiktokfitness #gymmotivation

text.description: Dumbbell Bent Over Rows Tutorial: Perfecting the Dumbbell Row Technique with Proper Form and Hinging.  I know the name is literally “Bent over Rows” but don’t just bend over. You start the movement by hinging and driving the hips back, soften your knees to lean your torso forward until it’s nearly parallel with the ground or just above.  Brace your core and think about keeping your back completely flat or a neutral spine. Then drive your elbows up or towards the ceiling leading with your back.  Keep your core and spine stable as you reverse the motion, extending your arms to lower the dumbbells so that they hang by your knees and repeat it again. text.description: 3 Fundamental terms you NEED to know about building muscle further explained👇 Progressive overload combines all the terms and is something you NEED to know in order to maximize your growth in the gym. How it works: Let's say you have 3 straight sets for bicep curls each with a rep range of 6-10 reps. The first set, you chose to do 20lbs and struggled to get 7 reps. The second set you did 20lbs and struggled to get 6 reps. The third set you did 20lbs and struggled to get 6 reps. You're near the bottom of your rep range (6-10), so you shoudn't increase the weight because your not strong enough yet. So bext time you do that same biceps exercise again, try and do more reps of the same weight. The day you're doing consistently 10 reps-ish on all three of your straight sets, you're ready to grab 22.5lbs and start that next session at the bottom of the rep range at 6 reps again. Rinse and repeat to get stronger and maximize growth. This is progressive overload. Apply it to ALL exercises and muscles!  #progressiveoverload #workout #fitnesstips

text.description: The age old question… What’s better the high bar or low bar squat? The real answer is it depends person to person but for training purposes you can utilize both depending on what areas need the most work. If you need to build your posterior chain more the low bar wide stance will be a better option. That doesn’t mean you need to adopt that for your squat of a lifetime stance.  If you need to build your legs more a narrow stance high bar is the move. If you’re training for BIG squats I would do your “competition stance” for maximal sets and the stance that targets your weaknesses more precisely for your secondary movement  #squat #highbarsquat #lowbarsquat #legs #legday #fitnesstips

text.description: A quick primer on how to spot ✅ vs. not spot ❌ different lifts 😁Spotting refers to supporting someone’s lift by ensuring that they can safely perform their repetitions. The goal is not to lift the weight for them as we often see, but rather to let them complete the set on their own as much as possible, stepping in to assist only when absolutely needed. The person spotting is known as the spotter. Today, I show you examples of 5 different examples of what NOT to do versus the correct way. Surprisingly, the incorrect ways are not exaggerations. I have either personally seen these scenarios play out with my own eyes, or clients and friends have had these happen to them. 😩Say no to inappropriate spotting 🙅🏻‍♀️Do you have any inappropriate spotting stories to share?#SpottingTechnique #FitnessTips

text.description: 🔽랫 풀다운(Lat PullDown)그립별 자극 차이 총정리🔽 🔸ROPE vs STANDARD vs UNDER vs BEHIND🔸 1. 로프 그립 (Rope Grip Pulldown) - 로프 손잡이를 이용해 팔꿈치를 뒤로 벌리며 당기면 후면 삼각근(Rear Delts)과 승모근(Mid/Lower Traps)에 집중됩니다. 2. 기본 그립 (Standard Straight Bar Grip) - 어깨너비의 바를 정면에서 당기면 광배근 전체(Lats)를 균형 있게 자극하며 초보자부터 상급자까지 가장 일반적이고 안정적인 등운동입니다. 3. text.description: You didn’t gain 2 lbs of fat overnight… To gain a pound of fat, you would need to be in a surplus of roughly 3500 calories. 5 x 3500 cals = 17,500 cals in one day. That’s a GNARLY food challenge that would require a lot of intention to accomplish, not eating a cookie one night 😂 There are SO many reasons that the scale can go up that is NOT fat gain: 👉Sodium. An excess of sodium causes you to hold water. 👉Sleep. Oversleeping OR undersleeping. 👉Stress. Stress increases cortisol & other fight-or-flight hormones that cause you to hold water. 👉Hard training session. The muscle cells are retaining more water for recovery. 👉Full glycogen stores.  1 gram of glycogen can hold 2-4 grams of water so when you eat carbohydrates and restore your glycogen levels, this can lead to an increase in scale weight that is actually advantageous. 👉Eating later than normal. It’s normal to wake up heavier after a night of later evening, simply because there is more food in your stomach. 👉Female hormone fluctuations. Need I say more😂 👉Sick. Inflammation is high to aid in recovery. 👉Lack of movement. This can also contribute to digestion changes. 👉Dehydration. Not drinking enough water can actually cause you to HOLD water. Before you go freak out and run to the elliptical to make up for the uptick in the scale (been there & done that too💁‍♀️) take inventory of ALLLL of the other things going on in your life before blaming it on your food! #fitness #nutrition #nutritiontips #FitTok #fitnesstips #fyp #foryoupage #weightloss #fitnesstransformation #fitnessjourney

text.description: 🔽 덤벨로 완성하는 가슴운동(Chest Workout) 5가지 🔽 🔸Minimal Equipment, Maximum Chest Gains🔥 1. 내로우 그립 덤벨 프레스 (Narrow-Grip Dumbbell Press) 손을 좁게 모아 덤벨을 밀어 올리면 가슴 안쪽 (Inner Chest) 에 집중 자극을 주어 중앙 라인을 선명하게 만듭니다. 2. 언더그립 덤벨 플라이 (Underhand Dumbbell Fly) 아래에서 위로 덤벨을 벌려 올리는 동작으로 가슴 상부 (Upper Chest) 에 자극을 주어 윗가슴 라인을 부각시킵니다. 3. 덤벨 풀오버 (Dumbbell Pullover) 머리 뒤로 덤벨을 넘기는 동작으로 가슴 중간 (Mid Chest) 과 하부 (Lower Chest) 를 동시에 늘리고 수축시킵니다. 4. 덤벨 프레스 (Flat Dumbbell Press) 가장 기본적인 프레스 동작으로 가슴 중앙 (Mid Chest) 을 균형 있게 발달시키는 데 효과적입니다. 5. 인클라인 덤벨 프레스 (Incline Dumbbell Press) 상체를 기울인 상태에서 덤벨을 밀어 올리면 가슴 상부 (Upper Chest) 에 자극을 집중시켜 윗가슴 볼륨을 살릴 수 있습니다. 📌 각 동작 3–4세트!   📌 천천히 내리고 강하게 수축! 📌 덤벨 하나면 어디서든 가슴운동 가능! #chestworkout #exercises #pushday #fitnesstips #chestday #오운완 #헬린이

text.description: **Dumbbell Incline Press** Hello, my fitness friends! Have you ever dreamed of pecs so chiseled, they could deflect flying ping pong balls? The Dumbbell Incline Press is here to transform those dreams into reality. First off, let's position our incline bench at either 15 or 30 degrees. Consider this your incline to success. (Quick tip: 30 degrees is the golden angle, optimal for really honing those pecs.) Puff up that chest like you're a proud bird flaunting its plumage. Not just for show, this sets the stage for an effective press.  Next, imagine tucking a secret treasure map behind you - retract those rear delts. This sets you up for an impeccable lift.  Here comes the shy part: turn your elbows in 45 degrees. It’s all about hitting those pecs from the right angle. Now, press up as if you're pushing against the sky, squeezing at the top like you're giving your muscles a well-deserved high-five! Now, are you ready to sculpt your chest with the Dumbbell Incline Press? Grab those weights, and let's hit those pecs! But before we dive in, I just wanted to express my gratitude. text.description: STRONG FOR SUMMER - HOME WORKOUT  50 sec work, 20 sec rest  heavy as you can go with perfect form 1. Heels elevated goblet squat 2. Reverse lunge left (glute bias - lean forward!) 3. Reverse lunge left (glute bias - lean forward!) 4. Lateral raises (crispy shoulders) 5. Tricep pushups (Hands under shoulders - shoot elbows back towards hips and bring chest forward to target back of arms) 6. Glute Bridge (banded + weighted) Go heavy! For these: do 50 sec bridge, 20 sec pulse. Then rest. Thank me later. 7. Tuck-in crunch or Jackknife - Pick your poison! Both HURT! Make sure your shoulders lift off the floor, and your hips pull in slightly for full engagement of your abs. Give yourself 2-3 hard working sets of each, 3x a week.  Repeating the same movement patterns and getting stronger at them is what brings results. Go get em!

text.description: Why your belly domes or bulges during exercise (and how to troubleshoot it) 👇 When you see doming, coning, or bulging, it’s just your body’s natural response to the list below. It’s feedback. And being able to figure out what might be causing it will help you change your core workouts and make them way more effective. Here are four common reasons this happens: 1. Your deep core isn’t fully engaging yet. Your pelvic floor, transverse abdominis, diaphragm, and multifidi all work as a team to manage pressure. When they’re not coordinating, pressure doesn’t get evenly distributed and pushes into the areas that are weakest. By learning to properly engage your deep core, you can fix this. 2. Your alignment needs some attention. When your ribs aren’t stacked over your pelvis, your diaphragm and pelvic floor can’t work together as well. Finding your neutral alignment is really important. This one is often really overlooked and it’s one of the easier ones to fix. 3. Your outer core muscles like to take over. If your six pack and obliques are stronger than your deep core, they’ll try to run the show. That’s when you see bread loafing or a V shape pushing your tummy up. This just means your deep core could use some extra love. 4. You have connective tissue changes. Diastasis recti or tissue changes from pregnancy or significant weight loss can create thinner areas where pressure naturally travels. Super common and also very workable. Continue to get stronger by appropriately challenging yourself with progressive overload and good form. Remember: these aren’t problems, they’re starting points. 💪  Code Jan26 will save you 15% off my app! #deepcore #diastasisrecti #momswholift #gymtips #coreworkout

text.description: 5 Exercises to Grow Your Abs  Abs are built in the gym. Just like any other muscle you have to train it hard and progressively overload it overtime. Having developed abs at a lower body fat percentage will make it look like you got bricks popping out of your stomach.  💥 Toes To Bar  💥 GHD Reverse Crunches 💥 Cable Crunches  💥 Incline Reverse Crunches  💥 Ab Rollouts All these exercises can be regressed and progressed to your experience level. GHD reverse crunches can be regressed by adjusting the pad distance. Toes to bar can be regressed to hanging knee raises. Ab rollouts can be regressed from standing to kneeling.  Cable crunches you can progress in with weight. Incline reverse crunches can be regressed by decreasing the bench incline. All great exercises to do to build your abs. I like doing 2-3 sets of 6-15 reps depending on the exercise. You could pick 3 exercises a week and do 3 sets on non consecutive days to really develop your abs.  @rawnutrition [code DYLAN] @gymshark [code DSHAN10] Training Plans in bio YouTube Channel “Dylan Shannon” @_dylanshannon on Instagram

text.description: Want to lose 10kg in 2 weeks?  Sure, I’ll tell you how to do it…  but you’re gonna destroy your body in the process.  1. Cut out all carbs. No potatoes, no rice, not even fruit. This depletes your glycogen, so you’ll drop weight fast. People go keto and drop 5kg overnight, right? But it’s all water weight, not real fat loss.  2. Work out twice a day—morning and evening. Mainly cardio, so you burn maximum calories. But guess what? This puts you in an insane calorie deficit, and you’re going to crash.  3. Fasting—one meal a day or every other day. Drink water, push through the hunger, load up on caffeine. But when you eat, keep it protein and veg.   Sure, you’ll lose weight, but you’re also frying your nervous system and messing up your hormones and metabolism.  Here’s the truth: This is a temporary fix.   You’ll drop weight, but the second you stop, the weight will come back—and then some.  Instead of wrecking your body, do it the right way. Eat in a small calorie deficit, get more walks in, and stay hydrated. This is how you get lasting results.  Want the REAL blueprint for fat loss that actually works long-term?  👉 DM ‘Fat Loss Bible’, and I’ll send you the step-by-step guide to get it right. #weightloss #fatloss #health #foryou #fyp #trending

text.description: Most people think the best fat loss workout is the one that leaves you destroyed. Sweating more. Suffering more. Being exhausted after every session. That’s not transformation. That’s fatigue. The best fat loss training does 3 things 👇 👉 Burns calories 👉 Preserves muscle 👉 Allows recovery This is why resistance training wins 👇 Because muscle changes everything: • Higher metabolism • Better insulin sensitivity • Better body composition • Better long-term fat loss And this is where people go wrong 👇 Too much cardio. Too much HIIT. Too much intensity. Eventually: 👉 Recovery collapses 👉 Hunger skyrockets 👉 Stress hormones rise 👉 Performance drops That’s why things like daily long-distance running or endless bootcamp classes often backfire. People become tired… not transformed. And no… 100 crunches will not burn belly fat. Fat loss is systemic. Not local. The goal is not maximum exhaustion. It’s creating a body that burns more, moves better, and maintains muscle while getting leaner. Lift weights. Walk more. Recover properly. Repeat consistently. That’s the real formula. text.description: Stretching and mobility are essential — not just before training, but every day. They help improve movement, support performance, and play a huge role in preventing injuries. The more I’ve learned to listen to my body, the more I’ve realised how important it is to take the time to slow down and feel what needs attention. Some areas hold tension, some feel tight, and others just need to move. Over time, I’ve found a simple floor routine that works for me — a way to check in with my body, stretch everything out, and create space before I train. It’s a small habit that’s made a big difference. Wearing the @Oner Active effortless seamless leggings in soft sage green 🤍 code: DESI #mobilitytraining #injuryprevention #trainwithintention
